I have a bunch of comments, but most are minor. You got a lot of complex stuff working here. Great start.

Could you make one semi-related change in your amended commit?

In the chassis.md file, It has the Type of the PresencePath property being a GPIO. That should be string instead right?

You should only use std::move() on objects of a class that contain resources and that you want to take ownership of or steal the resources from.

For gpioPins, this is correct because the parameter is by copy (no reference) and contains unique_ptrs (which cannot be copied without move). So you want to std::move a container of unique_ptrs that you are taking ownership of.

Similarly, presencePath is by copy (no reference), so it is smart to std::move it since you can steal the memory of the contained std::string.

For built-in types (int, float, bool, etc) and objects that you are not taking ownership of (such as a const std::string&), you don't need/want to to std::move().

The BMC coding conventions state enums need to start with a capital letter. So GPIODirection or GpioDirection. Same with the polarity enum name.

Based on the markdown doc, an example value will be "/dev/i2c-159". So I think all of this code is probably copy/paste and not correct for this app.

One suggestion would be to call parseString() and then do a little validation of the result.

For example, the first character should probably be a '/' right? The app needs an absolute path, since a relative path would be unclear/unusable. And a value with no slashes like "fred_jones" is really wrong.
